faqHeading: What people in OKC ask first.

faqs.q: What is the most common mistake people make ordering porta potties?
faqs.a: Ordering too few. People count guests or workers and forget hours. A unit that is fine for a two-hour party will be unusable by the end of a ten-hour festival day. Give us the timeline, not just the headcount.

faqs.q: Can a unit sit in the street in front of my house?
faqs.a: Not without checking first. Oklahoma City and the suburbs each have their own rules about putting anything in the public right-of-way. On your own driveway or yard there is normally nothing to arrange.

faqs.q: How do you keep units from blowing over?
faqs.a: Placement and anchoring. Units go on level ground out of the open, ideally in the lee of a building or a fence line, and are staked or strapped on exposed sites. Central Oklahoma wind takes over a unit that is just set down in a field.

faqs.q: Is a restroom trailer worth it for a wedding?
faqs.a: For an evening reception with older guests or formal clothes, usually yes. For a casual afternoon barbecue, a couple of upgraded units with sinks do the job for less.

faqs.q: Do I have to be home for delivery?
faqs.a: No. Mark the spot with a flag or send a photo of where you want it, and make sure the gate is open or the code is in your notes.

faqs.q: How fast can I get a unit?
faqs.a: It depends on the route schedule that week. Call with your address and date and you will get an actual answer instead of a promise.

pages.heading: Porta potties for construction in Oklahoma City.
pages.intro: For builders, remodelers, roofers and road crews. Dropped before the crew shows up, serviced every week, gone when the job is done.
pages.seoTitle: Construction Porta Potty Rental Oklahoma City | Red Dirt
pages.seoDescription: Job-site porta potty rental for builders and contractors in Oklahoma City, Edmond, Yukon and Mustang. Weekly service and OSHA-based unit counts.

sections.heading: Start from OSHA's table.
sections.body: 29 CFR 1926.51 is the federal rule for job-site toilets. Twenty workers or fewer: one toilet. Twenty to 199: a toilet seat and a urinal per 40 workers. Two hundred or more: a seat and a urinal per 50. That is the legal floor. If your crew works long days, or if subs rotate through and the headcount swings, size for the busy week rather than the average one.

sections.heading: Where the work is right now.
sections.body: The steady demand is residential: subdivisions going up in Edmond, Yukon, Mustang and Piedmont, where one unit per lot or one per cul-de-sac sits for the length of the build. Commercial jobs downtown and along the turnpikes run bigger orders for shorter stretches. Both are routine.

sections.heading: Put it where the truck can reach it all job long.
sections.body: The usual problem is not delivery day, it is week six, when the driveway is poured, the yard is graded and the unit is now behind a pallet of brick. Pick a spot near the curb or the site entrance that will stay reachable from start to finish.

faqs.q: Can I add a second unit mid-job?
faqs.a: Yes. Call when framing crews or finishers pile on, and it rides out on the next route.

faqs.q: What does weekly service actually cover?
faqs.a: Tank pumped, unit washed down, paper and sanitizer topped up. Extra visits can be added for big crews or summer heat.

pages.heading: Wedding and party porta potty rental in OKC.
pages.intro: Backyard weddings, graduation parties, reunions and church picnics. Clean units, sized to your guest list and placed where nobody has to look at them.
pages.seoTitle: Wedding & Party Porta Potty Rental OKC | Red Dirt
pages.seoDescription: Porta potty rental for weddings, graduation parties, reunions and backyard events in Oklahoma City, Edmond and Norman. Sized to your guest count.
pages.service: Wedding and party portable restroom rental

sections.heading: Guests, hours, and whether there is a bar.
sections.body: A working number for a party of about four hours is one unit per 50 guests. Stretch it to six hours and you want closer to one per 35. Add an open bar and go up again. So a 200-guest backyard wedding that runs from four to ten with drinks is not four units — it is more like six, or a trailer plus a couple of standard units for overflow.

sections.heading: Close, but behind something.
sections.body: The best spot is a short walk from the party, behind the tent, the barn or a row of trees — not in the background of every photo. Keep units away from the food and downwind of it. If the reception runs past sunset, a string of lights on the path saves a lot of phone flashlights.

sections.heading: Small changes guests notice.
sections.body: Units with an interior sink and mirror cost a little more and change how a backyard wedding feels. So does a hand-wash station placed next to standard units. For formal or evening events, look at a restroom trailer instead.

faqs.q: When do the units show up?
faqs.a: The day before or the morning of, and they are collected after the weekend. If your venue limits delivery times, tell us when you book.

faqs.q: We are getting married on a ranch outside the city. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Send a pin and describe the drive in — dirt, gravel, a cattle guard, a gate. The more we know, the smoother delivery day goes.

pages.heading: Luxury restroom trailers in Oklahoma City.
pages.intro: For receptions, galas, company events and anything where guests are dressed up. Flushing toilets, real sinks, lighting and climate control.
pages.seoTitle: Luxury Restroom Trailer Rental Oklahoma City | Red Dirt
pages.seoDescription: Luxury restroom trailer rental for weddings, galas and corporate events in Oklahoma City, Edmond and Norman. Flushing toilets, sinks and AC.

sections.heading: It is the difference guests remember.
sections.body: Standard units are fine for a ball game. At a reception in an Oklahoma July, guests in suits and long dresses notice the difference between a plastic box and an air-conditioned room with a mirror and a sink. A trailer is the one restroom upgrade people mention afterward.

sections.heading: Four things to confirm before you book.
sections.body: A flat place to park it. Room for a truck to back a trailer in — check gate widths, low limbs and soft turf. A power source within reach, usually a dedicated outlet or the caterer's generator. And whether you want an attendant, which is worth it for big guest lists and long nights.

sections.heading: Count stations, not trailers.
sections.body: Trailers are rated by stations — each toilet or urinal is one. Smaller trailers suit rehearsal dinners and small receptions; big weddings and corporate events need a larger trailer or a trailer backed up by a few standard units off to one side.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I reserve?
faqs.a: As soon as the date and venue are set. Trailers are limited and the spring and fall Saturdays go first.

faqs.q: Does it need a water line?
faqs.a: Usually not — most trailers carry their own fresh and waste tanks. Power is the one hookup you will need.

pages.heading: Handicap porta potty rental in Oklahoma City.
pages.intro: Roll-in accessible units for public events, parks, schools and job sites — and for any private party where a guest uses a wheelchair.
pages.seoTitle: Handicap Accessible Porta Potty Rental OKC | Red Dirt
pages.seoDescription: Handicap and wheelchair-accessible porta potty rental for events, parks and job sites in Oklahoma City, Edmond, Norman and Moore.

sections.heading: One in twenty, and never zero.
sections.body: When portable units are grouped at one spot, the 2010 ADA Standards require at least five percent of them to be accessible, with a minimum of one. A festival with twenty units needs at least one accessible unit; one with forty needs two. Event organizers and parks departments check for this.

sections.heading: Room to turn around.
sections.body: Accessible units sit flat on the ground with no step, have a wide door, grab bars on the walls and enough floor space to turn a wheelchair. Anyone can use them, which makes them a good single-unit choice for small gatherings too.

sections.heading: The path counts as much as the unit.
sections.body: Put it on firm, level ground with a clear route from where people are — not across gravel, up a slope or through wet grass. Leave a clear patch in front of the door so a chair can line up.

faqs.q: Can I order only accessible units?
faqs.a: Yes. Some customers do exactly that for family events, since every guest can use them.

pages.heading: Hand-washing stations for rent in Oklahoma City.
pages.intro: Freestanding sinks with water, soap and towels. No plumbing, no hose, nothing to hook up.
pages.seoTitle: Hand Washing Station Rental Oklahoma City | Red Dirt
pages.seoDescription: Portable hand-washing station rental for food vendors, fairs, ranches and job sites in Oklahoma City, Edmond, Norman and Moore.

sections.heading: Food, livestock and dirty work.
sections.body: Vendors at fairs and festivals, petting zoos and livestock shows, ranch events, and crews mixing concrete or handling chemicals. If the people on site touch food, animals or anything you would not want on a sandwich, they need somewhere to wash.

sections.heading: The health department sets the rule, not us.
sections.body: Food vendors usually need hand washing to get an event permit. The Oklahoma City-County Health Department and the event organizer decide what qualifies. Check with them before you order so the station you get is the one your permit asks for.

sections.heading: One station per cluster of units.
sections.body: A double-basin station next to a group of three or four porta potties covers most events. Food lines should have their own, separate from the restrooms.

faqs.q: Do they need power or a hose?
faqs.a: No. They carry their own fresh water and a gray-water tank, and are refilled at service.

sections.heading: Units that follow the rig.
sections.body: Locations in Canadian, Kingfisher, Grady and Logan counties need restrooms for the life of the job and often need them moved when the crew does. Give us the lease name, a pin and the gate combination, and say who signs for the site — the company man, the pusher or the office.

sections.heading: Pick a service day and forget about it.
sections.body: Long-term units run on a fixed weekly service day. Small crews at remote spots can sometimes stretch longer; large crews and July heat need more. Set it once and adjust only when the job changes.

sections.heading: Tell us what the road does when it rains.
sections.body: Red clay roads that are fine in August turn impassable after a storm. Say so up front, so the unit goes somewhere the service truck can still reach on a wet week.

faqs.q: How is a monthly rental billed?
faqs.a: Every four weeks for as long as the unit is out. Call for a quote on your location.

faqs.q: Can you move units between locations?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask before the next service day and the move is done on that run.

sections.heading: Game days burn through units.
sections.body: Tailgates run long, start early and involve a cooler. Plan more units than you would for a party of the same size — roughly one per 30 to 40 people for an all-day tailgate — and put a hand-wash station beside them.

sections.heading: Clear it with whoever runs the lot.
sections.body: Private lots, church lots and businesses near the stadium each have their own rules. Confirm with the owner where units can sit and when they have to be gone, then tell us so delivery and pickup fit inside that window.

sections.heading: Same idea, longer weekend.
sections.body: Softball, soccer and baseball tournaments that run Friday to Sunday need units serviced between days. Tell us the schedule and the fields, and the units are cleaned overnight.

faqs.q: Can units stay for a whole season of home games?
faqs.a: Yes. Season-long setups can stay in place and be serviced after each game.
